notes: Hard (14/30). Single focused structure-learning task: from telemetry samples alone, recover a directed tree DAG using three coupled heuristics — fixed-edge-count maximum-|Pearson| spanning tree via Prim with deterministic tie-breaks, unique-root constraint orienting every edge away from the root via BFS, and the sibling conditional-independence (child-analogy) rule resolving any residual directional ambiguity. Hidden cases change topology (chain, star, two-level tree), node count (5-7), root position, and column ordering, and deliberately include strong grandparent/grandchild correlations that break non-spanning-tree greedy scans and column-order shortcuts; the directed edge set is compared exactly, so one misresolved direction or one wrong skeleton edge fails. Rubric: high reasoning_depth (three interacting heuristics), debugging_ambiguity (direction resolution), hidden_case_generalization (fully generic solver), quantitative_correctness (exact set equality); modest tool breadth and one dependent stage. Difficulty >= competency floor (hard).
